Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market rose on the latest day, a short session after the holiday, but its mood stays stressed with the trend down. letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to sell, and the whole-market plan carries on as usual with this week's small buy. The market rose on the latest day, a short session after the holiday, but its mood stays stressed and the trend still points down. One good day after a holiday tells us little, so nothing is rushed. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The game stands at three weeks won and three lost, which is exactly what a coin would give. This week's bet is still ahead so far, but it is not scored until the week closes, and a lead can vanish.

Third, a lesson. A sailor does not change course every time the wind shifts for an hour. Steady hands get further than busy ones.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
